# OpenLRR hook / extension architecture — measured

Repo: `C:/Users/Pierce Lonergan/Documents/GitHub/DeepCoreOverhaul`

## 1. How a reimplemented function replaces the exe's

**The primitive.** `hook_write` (`src/openlrr/hook.cpp:76-103`) is the only thing that actually touches memory: `VirtualProtect(PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE)` → `memcpy` → `VirtualProtect(restore)`. Everything else is a byte-pattern generator on top of it.

Four generators, all in `src/openlrr/hook.cpp`, declared in `hook.h:27-59`:

| helper | bytes written | pattern | use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hook_write_jmp` (`hook.cpp:19`) | 5 | `E9 rel32` | **not used anywhere active** |
| `hook_write_jmpret` (`hook.cpp:36`) | **6** | `E9 rel32` + `C3` | the workhorse — whole-function replacement |
| `hook_write_call` (`hook.cpp:53`) | 5 | `E8 rel32` | replace one individual `CALL` site |
| `hook_write_addr` (`hook.cpp:71`) | 4 | absolute pointer | repoint an import thunk's function-pointer slot |

`hook_write_jmpret(address, jmpAddress)` overwrites the **first 6 bytes of the exe function's prologue** with a relative `JMP` to the DLL's C++ implementation, plus a trailing `RET`. The distance is computed by `hook_to_dist` (`hook.cpp:9-12`) as `dst - (src + 5)`.

Three consequences that define the whole project's engineering envelope:

- **It is destructive, not a trampoline.** The original prologue is gone. `hook_write_jmpret` takes an `OPTIONAL uint8* backup` but the restore path is commented out (`hook.cpp:30-32, 47-49`), and nothing in the tree ever passes a backup. **There is no way to call the original implementation.** A reimplementation must be complete, not a wrapper.
- **The calling convention must match exactly.** The C++ function inherits the caller's stack frame verbatim; hence the pervasive `__cdecl` on every reimplemented function.
- **The target need not be a function entry.** `Camera_ToggleFreeMovement` is hooked at `0x00435cc1` (`interop.cpp:2892`) — an odd, mid-function address. This is how OpenLRR reaches code the compiler inlined.

**When it's installed.** Two distinct phases:

1. **DLL attach.** `DllMain`/`DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH` → `InjectOpenLRR` (`dllmain.cpp:43` → `OpenLRR.cpp:59`). This detects *how* the DLL got loaded by byte-comparing the exe (`OpenLRR.cpp:67-79`): `EB FE` at `PROCESS_EIP` (0x0048f2c0) ⇒ `InjectMethod::Injector`; a normal `55 8B EC FF 74 24` prologue at `PROCESS_WINMAIN` (0x00477a60) ⇒ `InjectMethod::DllStart` (**returns early — WinMain is left alone**); otherwise `DllImport`, and it calls `interop_hook_WinMain()` (`interop.cpp:174-178`) which jmprets `LegoRR.exe!WinMain` → `StartOpenLRRInjected`.
2. **Inside WinMain.** `LaunchOpenLRR` (`OpenLRR.cpp:1066`) calls `Gods98::Main_Initialise`, opens the console, then **`interop_hook_all()` at `OpenLRR.cpp:1095`** — every other hook in the program is installed there, in one shot, before `Gods98::Main_WinMain` runs.

`interop_hook_all` (`interop.cpp:4454-4580`) is deliberately ordered: `// First patch in merged functions and individual calls: Do this now to prevent messing up any jmpret function hooks (that contain calls being individually hooked).` (`interop.cpp:4458-4460`). Call-site patches go first (`4463-4466`), then all whole-function jmprets.

**Constants:** `PROCESS_EIP = 0x0048f2c0`, `PROCESS_WINMAIN = 0x00477a60` (`interop.h:6-7`), duplicated in `openlrr-injector.cpp:23-24` and `openlrr-makeexe.cpp:35`.

**The three launch paths** (this matters — they are not equivalent):
- `openlrr-injector` (`src/openlrr-injector/openlrr-injector.cpp:200-360`): `CreateProcess(CREATE_SUSPENDED)` → patch entrypoint to `EB FE` (infinite self-jump, line 262) → `ResumeThread` → `Sleep(100)` → `CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibrary, "openlrr-d.dll")` → **spin-wait polling `PROCESS_WINMAIN` until the hook lands** (lines 326-335) → restore the entrypoint.
- `openlrr-makeexe` (`src/openlrr-makeexe/README.md`, `openlrr-makeexe.cpp:400-448`): statically rewrites `LegoRR.exe` into `OpenLRR.exe` — inserts an `.idata2` PE section importing `openlrr.dll!StartOpenLRR`, and overwrites `WinMain` with `PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / 4× PUSH [ESP+0x14] / CALL [thunk] / ADD ESP,0x10 / POP EBP / RET 0x10`. This is the **`DllStart` path**, and it's why `InjectOpenLRR` returns early rather than double-patching.
- Plain `LoadLibrary` into a running LegoRR.exe ⇒ `DllImport`, patches WinMain at runtime.

**Sibling technique worth knowing about — "merged functions."** MSVC COMDAT-folded identical bodies in the 1999 build, so one address serves several logical functions. Those *cannot* be jmpret-hooked; each call site is patched instead. See `interop.cpp:305-321` and `832-856`: `AnimClone_IsLws` and `Flic_GetWidth` share one address; OpenLRR patches `hook_write_call` at `0x00473f60` for the AnimClone caller and at `0x004120f7 / 0x0045ab17 / 0x0045cfc8` for the three Flic callers. `// THIS FUNCTION MUST BE HOOKED ON AN INDIVIDUAL BASIS` (`interop.cpp:310`). Also `interop.cpp:3918`: `/// THIS IS A MERGED FUNCTION! DON'T HOOK!` (`RadarMap_Free`), and `interop.cpp:1572`: `// DO NOT HOOK: used by: Files.c (shared function call with Files.c!File_Error)`.

**And a fifth technique — raw assembly splicing.** `interop_hook_replace_LegoRR_PanelRadarMapZoom` (`interop.cpp:4401-4448`) NOP-slides two byte ranges inside the un-decompiled `Panel_CheckCollision` (`0x0045b291-0x0045b2d1`, `0x0045b2d8-0x0045b318`) and hand-assembles `MOV EAX,[ESP+0x14] / PUSH EAX / CALL <C++ fn> / ADD ESP,4` in their place. The stated rationale: *"the Panel_CheckCollision function is really large, and taking the time to decompile it will be a hassle"* (`interop.cpp:4405-4406`). This is the escape hatch for changing behaviour inside a function you don't want to reimplement.

## 2. The decompilation frontier, quantified

**Method.** A not-yet-implemented function is a live macro `#define X ((<sig>)0x00......)`; when implemented, the macro is commented out and a real declaration is uncommented directly beneath it (see `Game.h:1474-1475`, `Panels.h:196` vs `Panels.h:208`).

Reproducible commands (Git Bash, from repo root):

```bash
LIVE='^[[:space:]]*#define[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]+\(\('
IMPL='^[[:space:]]*//[[:space:]]*#define[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]+\(\('

for d in $(find src/openlrr -type d | sort); do
  files=$(find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cpp' \))
  [ -z "$files" ] && continue
  a=$(grep -Eh "$LIVE" $files | wc -l); b=$(grep -Eh "$IMPL" $files | wc -l)
  printf "%-30s live=%-4d impl=%-4d\n" "$d" $a $b
done

grep -rEh "$LIVE" --include=*.h --include=*.cpp src | wc -l   # 876
grep -rEh "$IMPL" --include=*.h --include=*.cpp src | wc -l   # 921
```

## 4. Adding brand-new game logic — the mechanical procedure

**The seam that makes everything possible:** the entire game main loop is already C++. `Lego_Initialise` (`GameState.cpp:94`), `Lego_MainLoop` (`GameState.cpp:885`), `Lego_Shutdown_Quick/Full` (`1861`/`1869`), `Lego_HandleKeys` (`1994`). They are installed as the Gods98 `Main_State` in `OpenLRR.cpp:1055-1061`, wrapped by `OpenLRR_Initialise_Wrapper` / `_MainLoop_Wrapper` / `_Shutdown_Wrapper` (`OpenLRR.cpp:958-994`), which carry explicit `// pre-MainLoop code here...` / `// post-MainLoop code here...` comment slots. **New per-frame logic goes there or in `GameState.cpp`, and needs no hook at all.**

### Procedure A — replace an existing exe function (the common case)
1. Find the live macro in the header, e.g. `Game.h:1474`.
2. Comment the macro, uncomment the declaration beneath it.
3. Write the body in the matching `.cpp`, tagged `// <LegoRR.exe @0042d030>`, with exact `__cdecl` signature.
4. Add `result &= hook_write_jmpret(0x0042d030, LegoRR::Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes);` to the module's `interop_hook_LegoRR_*` function, **only if** an un-decompiled exe function still calls it. If every caller is C++, leave it commented with `// internal, no need to hook these`.
5. If the address is a merged function → do **not** jmpret; patch each `CALL` site with `hook_write_call`.

### Procedure B — pure new behaviour (no exe function involved)
1. New state goes in **module-level `static`s in the DLL** or in a `*_Globs2` struct. Two exist: `Gods98::Main_Globs2` (`engine/Main.h:247-271`, instance `Main.cpp:77`) and `LegoRR::Lego_Globs2` (`Game.h:726-743`, instance `Game.cpp:154`, commented `/// CUSTOM: Extension of Lego_Globs for OpenLRR-exclusive globals`, `Game.h:766`). Never widen the exe-overlaid `Lego_Globs` (`Game.h:462`, `assert_sizeof(..., 0xf00)` at `Game.h:672`).
2. Per-object side tables use STL keyed on the exe pointer — the canonical example is `static std::map<LegoObject*, Debug_RouteVisual*> _routeVisuals;` (`game/Debug.cpp:69`), driven from `GameState.cpp:1158`.
3. Getter/setter pairs on the `Cheat_*` model: `Game.cpp:191-256` over `static bool _cheatNoBuildCosts` etc. (`Game.cpp:155-160`), consumed inside already-hooked functions (`Stats.cpp:864,872`; `Object.cpp:5868`).
4. Wire UI in `OpenLRR_UpdateMenuItems` (`OpenLRR.cpp:153-307`) + `OpenLRR_HandleCommand`, and a resource ID in `resources/resource.h`.

### Where OpenLRR already adds behaviour the exe never had — the sanctioned patterns

There are **683 `/// CUSTOM:` markers** across the tree (`grep -rh "CUSTOM:" --include=*.h --include=*.cpp src/openlrr | wc -l`), densest in `engine/Main.h` (60), `engine/Main.cpp` (46), `game/Game.h` (39). Use that marker on anything you add. Concrete precedents:

- **Shortcuts / rebindable input** — `game/Shortcuts.hpp` + `.cpp` (1,098 lines, **zero** exe addresses). Its own config file `Settings\Shortcuts.cfg` (`Shortcuts.hpp:22`), loaded via `Gods98::Config_Load2(..., FILE_FLAG_EXEDIR|FILE_FLAG_NOCD)` at `Shortcuts.cpp:380`, with a graceful `"…file not found, reverting to default keybinds."` fallback (`Shortcuts.cpp:442`). Consumed from game logic as `Shortcut_IsDown(ShortcutID::Cheat_FasterUnit)` (`Game.cpp:312`). **This is the template for any new user-facing config surface.**
- **Command line layer** — `cmdline/CommandLine.cpp` + `CLGen.cpp` (616 lines, zero exe addresses), feeding `Gods98::Main_CommandLineOptions` (`engine/Main.h:274+`) with `std::optional<T>` fields (`-nointro`, `-novideo`, `-log`, `-pos`, `-res`, `-bpp`, …). Read at `OpenLRR.cpp:1015` (`mainOptions.gameName`), `1073` (`mainOptions.log`), `1117` (`mainOptions.menu`).
- **Debug/cheat system menu** — `OpenLRR.cpp:112-307`. ~120 menu IDs across `&Options`/`&Debug`/`&Cheats`, `static_assert`-tied to engine enums (`OpenLRR.cpp:125-128`), loaded from the *DLL's* resources (`OpenLRR.cpp:1108-1109`), with a window callback override (`OpenLRR.cpp:1119`).
- **Route visualiser** — `game/Debug.h/.cpp`, an entire new subsystem (containers, meshes, per-object state) with no exe counterpart.
- **Gameplay tweaks inside hooked functions** — `Panel_RadarMap_ZoomIn/Out` (`Panels.cpp:26-38`, `maxZoom 20→30`, `minZoom 10→4`); `Weapon_Initialise`'s `/// SANITY: Memzero` and `/// FIX APPLY: ZERO OUT MEMORY SO THAT WE DON'T GET THE DISCHARGE GLITCH WITH POWER BEAM` (`Weapons.cpp:41,62,74`); wobbly-world (`OpenLRR.cpp:940-951`); topdown fog, FP controls in topdown, resource tumble, custom CryOre colours (`Lego_Globs2`, `Game.h:729-742`).
- **Unbounded replacements for fixed exe arrays** — `static std::vector<Point2I> _drainPowerBlockList / _poweredBlockList / _unpoweredBlockList;` with the comment `// PowerGrid replacements for infinite grid sizes.` (`Game.cpp:165-168`). **This is the proven escape from a fixed-size exe table.**

### Your three specific examples

- **New creature ability** — cheapest of the three. `object/Creature.h` is **100% implemented (24/24)**, `object/Building.h` 24/24, `object/Vehicle.h` 29/29, `world/Construction.h` 32/32. Add C++ inside already-hooked bodies + a `Lego_Globs2` / static-map flag. The friction is `object/AITask.h` at **9/105 (9%)** — if the ability needs a new AI *task* rather than a new effect on an existing one, you are decompiling AITask first.
- **Per-weapon visual** — `object/Weapons.h` is **48/48 implemented**, `WeaponStats` is heap-allocated from the cfg count (`Weapons.cpp:56-60`), and `Weapon_Initialise`/`Weapon_Update` are called from C++ (`GameState.cpp:566, 1078`) so they're not even hooked. `Weapon_Lazer_Add` (`Weapons.cpp:816-833`) hardcodes two meshes with literal colours `(0.6,0.6,0.6,1.0)` and `(0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0)` and `timer = 5.0f`. Adding a per-weapon appearance means: extend `WeaponStats` with new fields **(safe — heap struct, no `assert_sizeof`… but see §5)**, parse them in `Weapon_Initialise`, thread the weapon index into `Weapon_Lazer_Add`. **This is a clean, self-contained job.** The one hard constraint is `Weapon_Globs` itself: `assert_sizeof(Weapon_Globs, 0x1b90)` at `Weapons.h:140`, overlaid at `0x00504870` (`Weapons.cpp:27`), with `lazerList[WEAPON_MAXLAZERS=10]` inline (`Weapons.h:31,135`) — 10 simultaneous beams is fixed unless you replace `lazerList` with a DLL-side container.
- **New UI panel** — **the expensive one.** `interface/Panels.h` is **0/52** and `interface/Interface.h` is **3/99**. `Panel_Initialise`, `Panel_CreateButtons`, `Panel_Draw`, `Panel_CheckCollision`, `Panel_LoadImage` are all raw addresses. There is no seam; you would be reimplementing the panel subsystem (~50 functions) or resorting to the assembly-splice technique of `interop.cpp:4401`. Budget accordingly.

## 5. Risk model, and the rule

The danger is not the hooking — it is the **124 struct overlays** onto the exe's data segment (`grep -rn '= \*(.*\*)0x00' --include=*.cpp src/openlrr | wc -l`), guarded by **394 `assert_sizeof` static-asserts** (`common.h:207`). Every one is a hard-coded absolute address with a hard-coded size: `statsGlobs` at `0x00503bd8` sized `0x5b0` (`Stats.cpp:41`, `Stats.h:232`); `legoGlobs` at `0x005570c0` sized `0xf00` (`Game.cpp:151`, `Game.h:672`); `weaponGlobs` at `0x00504870` sized `0x1b90` (`Weapons.cpp:27`, `Weapons.h:140`).

The `static_assert` catches a *size* change at compile time. It does **not** catch a field-order change, and it does **not** catch you enlarging an inner array while shrinking padding. Those compile clean and corrupt the neighbouring global at runtime.

### Risk tiers

**GREEN — pure C++, no memory-layout consequence.**
- Editing the body of an already-implemented, already-hooked function.
- New DLL-side statics, `std::map`/`std::vector` side tables (`Debug.cpp:69`; `Game.cpp:165-168`).
- New fields on `Main_Globs2` / `Lego_Globs2` — these are DLL-owned (`Main.cpp:77`, `Game.cpp:154`), sizeless, and safe to grow indefinitely.
- New `Shortcuts` IDs, new `Main_CommandLineOptions` fields, new menu items.
- New files under `cmdline/`, `platform/`, or a new `game/` module with no exe counterpart.

**AMBER — verify before you commit.**
- Implementing a new exe function + adding its hook. Risk is *behavioural*, not structural: you must be complete (no trampoline exists), the signature must be byte-exact, and you must confirm the address isn't merged. Always cross-check the `// used by:` annotation already sitting above the hook line.
- Extending a **heap-allocated** struct (`WeaponStats`, `ObjectStats`) — safe *only if* every allocation site is C++. `WeaponStats` qualifies (`Weapons.cpp:56-60`). `ObjectStats` qualifies (`Stats.cpp:146`, sized `LegoObject_ID_Count * sizeof(ObjectStats*)` inside the C++ `Stats_Initialise`). **If any exe function still allocates or `sizeof`s it, you get a heap overrun with no diagnostic.**
- Touching a function annotated `// internal, no need to hook these` — re-check whether an exe caller crept back in.

**RED — do not, without a full-tree audit.**
- Changing any field of a struct that carries an `assert_sizeof` and is bound to a fixed address. Adjusting the `assert_sizeof` number to make the build pass is the single most destructive edit available in this repo — `Stats_Globs` ends at `0x504188`, `textGlobs` begins at `0x504190`; there are **8 bytes of slack**, and `LegoObject_ID_Count 15→16` would run 72 bytes into `Text_Globs`.
- Raising `LegoObject_ID_Count` (`GameCommon.h:1143`) or `LegoObject_Type_Count`. Both are load-bearing across at least 13 fixed-layout tables: `Stats.h:228`, `Object.h:454,463,464`, `AITask.h:147`, `Dependencies.h:91`, `Interface.h:143`, `HelpWindow.h:91-93`, `Weapons.h:83`.
- `hook_write_jmpret` onto a merged address (`interop.cpp:310, 1572, 1766, 1920, 3918`).
- Anything in `#pragma region Temporary Hooks` — `interop.cpp:4574-4576` says `// Do not commit anything in here!`.
- Byte-splicing new assembly into an un-decompiled function without the `Panel_RadarMap_ZoomIn` treatment (NOP-slide the *whole* range first, `interop.cpp:4427-4429`).

### The rule

> **The exe owns memory layout; the DLL owns behaviour.**
>
> You may freely add code, and you may freely add state — but every byte of new state must live in DLL-owned storage (a `*_Globs2`, a file-scope `static`, an STL container, or a heap struct whose every allocation is C++). If a change would alter the size, field order, or array extent of anything carrying `assert_sizeof` and a `*(T*)0x00......` address, it is out of bounds. **If you find yourself editing a number inside `assert_sizeof`, stop.**
>
> Corollary for hooks: never hook an address without reading the `// used by:` comment above it, and never hook one flagged merged — patch its call sites instead.

---

## 6. Reimplementing `Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes` — hard, not a dead end

**It is more tractable than it looks, and here is the decisive fact: no hook is required.**

The five loaders are called from `Lego_Initialise`, which is *already* fully C++:

```
GameState.cpp:507-509
    if (Lego_LoadLighting() && Lego_LoadGraphicsSettings() && Lego_LoadUpgradeTypes() &&
        Lego_LoadVehicleTypes() && Lego_LoadMiniFigureTypes() && Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes() &&
        Lego_LoadBuildingTypes())
```

Today those five identifiers resolve to the macros at `Game.h:1466-1483`, so the C++ calls jump straight into the exe. Comment the macro, uncomment `//bool32 __cdecl Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes(void);` (`Game.h:1475`), write the body at the pre-staged slot `Game.cpp:3254`, and **the call site at `GameState.cpp:508` re-binds to your C++ function at compile time.** No `interop.cpp` entry needed at all. `grep -rn Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes` confirms `GameState.cpp:508` is the *only* call site in the tree.

This is not speculation — it is exactly the shape of `Weapon_Initialise`, whose hook is deliberately commented out at `interop.cpp:4345` precisely because its sole caller is `GameState.cpp:566`.

**What it actually requires.**

1. **Decompiling `0x0042d030` from Ghidra**, plus a chain of its callees still living at raw addresses in `Game.h` — notably `Lego_GetObjectByName` (`0x0042e7e0`, `Game.h:1511`), `Lego_GetObjectTypeIDCount` (`0x0042ee70`, `Game.h:1519`), and `Lego_LoadObjectNames` (`0x0042d530`, `Game.h:1486`). Realistically you decompile the whole `Lego_Load*Types` family together, since they share model-loading helpers.
2. **The destination is mostly heap, not fixed layout.** This is the good news. In `Lego_Globs`: `CreatureModel* rockMonsterData` at offset `0x11c`, `char** rockMonsterName` at `0x130`, `char** langRockMonster_name` at `0x19c`, `char** langRockMonster_theName` at `0x1b0`, `uint32 rockMonsterCount` at `0x1c4` (`Game.h:533-555`). Those are **pointers**. Writing them from C++ costs nothing structurally, and `Lego_Globs` stays `0xf00`.
3. **You need `Lego_GetObjectTypeIDCount` implemented too**, because `Object.cpp:252` already reads `const uint32 objIDCount = Lego_GetObjectTypeIDCount(objType); // LegoObject_ID_Count;` — the code is already written to be count-driven rather than assuming 15.

**What breaks / what stays broken.**

- **Reimplementing the loader alone does not raise the 15-ID ceiling, and it is not the thing standing in the way.** The ceiling is the fixed-layout tables (§5 RED), not the loader. A C++ loader that writes 16 rock monsters into `rockMonsterName` (heap — fine) would immediately overflow `statsGlobs.objectLevels[20][15]` (`Stats.h:228`), `objectTtSFX[20][15]` (`Object.h:454`), `Dependencies.table[20][15]` (`Dependencies.h:91`), `Interface.objectBools[20][15]` (`Interface.h:143`), `AITask.requestObjCounts[20][15][16]` (`AITask.h:147`), and `WeaponStats.objectCoefs[20][15][16]` (`Weapons.h:83`) — six struct overlays, several with only single-digit byte slack behind them.
- **The genuine escape route exists and is already proven in-tree.** Those six tables are reachable *only* via `statsGlobs`/`objectGlobs`/`dependencyGlobs`/`interfaceGlobs`/`aiGlobs`/`weaponGlobs`. `Stats_Globs.objectStats` is already `ObjectStats**` — a heap-of-heaps allocated by the C++ `Stats_Initialise` (`Stats.cpp:146`). The pattern for the *inline* tables is the one at `Game.cpp:165-168`: keep the exe struct byte-identical, ignore the inline array, and mirror it into a DLL-side `std::vector`/`std::map` that every C++ accessor reads instead. That works **for each table only once every function that touches it is implemented in C++**. Today: `Weapons.h` 48/48 ✅, `Stats` ✅ (`Stats_Initialise` at `Stats.cpp:124`, hooked `interop.cpp:4096`), but `AITask.h` **9/105** ❌, `Interface.h` **3/99** ❌, `Dependencies.h` **0/11** ❌.

**Verdict.** Reimplementing `Lego_LoadRockMonsterTypes` itself: **hard but well-scoped, a few hundred lines, zero interop risk, and structurally safe** — it writes to heap pointers only. Using it to exceed 15 IDs: **blocked, but by a different and enumerable obstacle** — `Dependencies` (11 fns), `Interface` (96 fns), and `AITask` (96 fns) must be decompiled first so their fixed `[20][15]` tables can be swapped for DLL-side storage. Not a dead end; a ~200-function prerequisite. Meanwhile the ~4 free RockMonster slots require **no** new code at all — `Stats_Initialise` (`Stats.cpp:124-851`) already reads them from cfg, and loose files override WADs.
